points.text: Closest multi-turn/agent baselines (Reflexion, Agent-Pro, OPRO, PromptAgent) cited but not compared.
Novelty of experience replay versus history-conditioned optimisers like OPRO and ExpeL not argued.
RL vocabulary is analogy only; value function and gamma undefined, no TD update.
Long-term planning claim is not measured or tested.
Predicted user emotion and success forecasts never validated or ablated.
Gains attributed to TD feedback but come mostly from replay, which baselines lack.
Feedbacker inputs differ across methods; TD gets user goal and API calls.
Main tables lack sample size, seeds, intervals; significance never tested despite small differences.
Protocol details missing: LLM roles, baseline reruns, reported epoch, user simulator.
Efficiency and cost claims unmeasured; optimisation cost not reported.
No self-refine baseline such as Reflexion in any table.
Human evaluation small, no agreement, blinding or significance; possible rater overlap.
Reported +54.2% is mean of per-LLM gains, misleading.
Typo 'believe setting'; Fig. 5 segment order not stated.
Code promised but not released.
Central comparison uncontrolled: most gain from replay, baselines lack it.
Long-term planning framing broader than shown; not measured.
Efficiency claim not measured.
Tables give single numbers without sample size or error bars.
Protocol (splits, N, epochs, roles) not presented in one place.
Delta% column easy to misread as gain of the mean.
Typos: 'believe setting', 'Converage Analysis'.
Simulated users assumed to represent real users; same simulator optimises and scores; simulator unnamed.
Deployment costs of per-turn feedback and growing replay context not discussed.
Prompt drift or regression across epochs in online deployment not studied.
Medical advice safety not scored separately; ethics statement inadequate.
Emotion-as-reward validity across languages and domains untested.
Typo 'believe setting'.
Main-text Fig. 4a covers only one system (Gemini).
Replay given only to RPO; TD-vs-MC gap within plausible noise.
Richer feedbacker inputs given only to RPO; need information-matched baselines.
Cost and latency reduction claims have no measurement.
No self-refine (Reflexion-style) baseline.
Long-term planning not measured; prompt may just fix slot/API errors.
Eq. 3 is analogy; V approximated by text feedback, gamma undefined.
No sample size or seeds for main tables; baselines differ within noise.
Medical study: n inconsistency, no agreement/blinding, possible rater overlap, insignificant margins.
Claims 'consistently surpass' and robustness overstated; false for Llama-70B.
+54.2% is mean of per-LLM relative gains, dominated by two models.
System-LLM and meta-LLM variation never crossed; medical uses one model.
Typos: 'believe setting', 'Converage Analysis'.
Unclear what practitioners should do when feedback is not useful.
No qualitative analysis of generated feedback.
Scaling and API cost unclear for longer trajectories with per-step feedback.
Limited theoretical analysis; no formal link of RPO to state, action, value.
Quality of feedbacker and reasonableness of generated rewards/values not studied.
No comparison with RL-based prompt methods such as StablePrompt.
No quantitative comparison of API calls or tokens versus APO/GPO.
High variance; no standard deviations in Tables 1 and 2.
No ablation replacing or analysing Feedbacker and Rewriter individually.
Insufficient explanation of prompts used to generate text gradients.
LLM feedback to adjust prompts widely explored (Self-Refine, Reflexion); limited novelty.
Effect of base model choice for feedbacker and rewriter unclear.
Unclear epochs, data volume and update timeliness needed in live systems.

P.summary: Missing multi-turn/self-refine baselines (Reflexion, Agent-Pro, OPRO).
Novelty of replay vs history-conditioned optimisers not argued.
RL/TD formulation is analogy, not theory.
Long-term planning claim not measured.
Emotion and success forecasts not validated.
Replay confound: gains from replay that baselines lack.
Feedbacker inputs not information-matched across methods.
No sample sizes, seeds, intervals or significance tests.
Experimental protocol details missing.
Efficiency/cost claims unmeasured; costs not reported.
Human medical evaluation small and under-described.
Delta% average reporting misleading.
Typos and caption issues.
Code not released.
Reliance on simulated users; sim-to-real gap.
Prompt drift/regression in online updates not studied.
Medical safety not evaluated separately.
Main-text training curve shows only one system.
Overclaiming consistent superiority and robustness.
System-LLM and meta-LLM variation not crossed.

Q.summary: No guidance when feedback is not useful.
No analysis of feedback quality or generated rewards.
No ablation of Feedbacker and Rewriter components.
Effect of base model choice for feedbacker/rewriter unclear.
Limited novelty vs Self-Refine and Reflexion.
